newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Bekaa voter turnout highest in election.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Bekaa voter turnout highest in election.

text.p: Voter turnout in Lebanon's eastern Bekka valley in the last round of Lebanon's general elections was higher than in any other region, Interior Minister Michel al-Murr said in remarks published on Monday.
Official results were expected later on Monday.
Murr told reporters late on Sunday that 210,840 people out of a total 408,770 eligible voters -- or about 52 percent -- cast ballots in the fifth round of voting.

The interior ministry had said shortly after polls closed at 5 p.m. (1400 GMT) that a preliminary count showed only about 37 percent of eligible voters cast their ballots in the Bekaa to elect 23 representatives to the 128-member parliament.
But Beirut newspapers said voting was extended by as much as two hours at some polling stations due to a last-minute surge.
Voter turnout varied between 31 percent and 48 percent in other regions.
